A minor race of sophonts resembling ambulatory sea slugs.

Three pseudopods, used to manipulate objects and to move on land
Communicate by whistling
Four sexes: male, female, neuter and incubator
Had just reached TL1 when they were enslaved by the Vargr

Notes

session-2026-08-02.title: Session 2026-08-02
session-2026-08-02.content:
traveller sota session
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
Session date: 2026-08-02
Starting in-fiction date: 193-1105
Starting position
The session resumed immediately after the attack at Dancado. Iaros Ujinka had been shot through the upstairs lounge window, the power and security drone had been taken out, and the third shooter remained outside and unidentified. Of the two intruders who entered the house, one was dead and the other unconscious. Kostas Backett was badly wounded at END 0 and STR 3. A grav car believed to belong to the POC was outside.
Live notes

The power was still out, so the upstairs autodoc would not work
Ozy ran to the ground-floor utility room to try to restore power
Admiral Cassius began tying up the unconscious intruder
Kostas Backett and StClair entered the exposed upstairs lounge to retrieve Ujinka, moving carefully in case the sniper still had a line of fire
As Kostas and StClair entered the lounge, they saw a grav car flying away. They thought it bore POC colours, but the identification was unconfirmed
Kostas and StClair got Ujinka to the autodoc, but it was too late to revive her
StClair treated Kostas’s injuries and restored 1 END, bringing him to END 1
Ozy began searching Ujinka’s library for notes relevant to her research
Admiral Cassius began calling Chief Inspector Pallod Norrim to report the situation
The crew planned to search the other rooms before the authorities arrived
With the authorities almost at Dancado, the crew began bringing the unconscious intruder around so they could question him first
The questioning produced little, but the intruder mentioned Ven Yasha. What connection Yasha has to the attack was not established
The arriving officers said they were the only POC personnel in the area and believed the crew had mistaken the identity of the grav car seen leaving
After dealing with the authorities at Dancado, the crew headed back to the Regina Down TAS Hostel
Ozy recovered data from Ujinka’s house concerning her Ancients research, Uncle Vlen, and the G-band work. The GM gave no specific contents yet, but the data may become useful later
The crew decided to remain at the hostel and try to repair Vlen’s smashed comms device
Kostas tried to use being shot to win sympathy from Zena Antonia, but it did not work
Ozy made some progress repairing Vlen’s smashed comms, but completing the repair will take several attempts
The crew returned to the commercial-district alleys to find Darrian Jak, but learned that the police had apparently picked him up earlier that day
Pallod Norrim called Kostas and said the POC had arrested Darrian Jak for Vlen’s murder. Pallod confirmed that Jak is a short redhead
Kostas asked Pallod about the suspected POC grav car, the connection to Ujinka’s shooting, and the attackers’ apparent ability to disable systems in a localised area. Pallod dismissed everything as coincidence and nothing to worry about, then quickly ended the call. Kostas found this very suspicious
Kostas left a message with Pallod’s secretary thanking him for closing the investigation and asking for an opportunity to face his uncle’s alleged killer
The crew went to bed. The following day, they were due to meet Detective Odoy that night
During the day, Ozy continued working on the smashed comms, Kostas researched Vlen’s unexplained age, and Admiral Cassius used his network to build influence on Regina beyond Pallod
Before the smashed comms became fully damaged, Ozy recovered the last number called from the device. It belongs to Winter Shipping, a logistics company operating in both Credo City and Star Town
Kostas found nothing new about Vlen’s true age
Admiral Cassius’s network reported that a ship called the Alahir arrived at Regina Highport several weeks ago. It is registered to the Scout Service but is not a standard scout design
The Alahir’s captain reportedly held numerous meetings with Pallod Norrim, and offworlders have reportedly been seen operating in POC uniforms since the ship arrived
The local POC are reportedly angry that an Imperial police force has taken over a murder inquiry
Rumour says the murdered man was a Zhodani spy and that the inquiry has become a matter of state security. The source did not establish the victim’s identity or confirm the rumour
Star Town is a thin strip between Credo City and Atora
An existing Winter Shipping advert offers to buy cargo from crews struggling with mortgage payments, salaries, or repairs, promising “Prompt service. No questions asked.”


Decisions and discoveries

One of the two intruders survived, mentioned Ven Yasha during questioning, and then entered POC custody
The suspected POC grav car left immediately after the attack rather than intervening; its identity and role remain unconfirmed
Ujinka is confirmed dead; the autodoc revival attempt was too late
The crew chose to notify the POC through Pallod before the authorities arrived
The surviving intruder connected the name Ven Yasha to the situation, but gave no clear explanation of his role
The POC deny having another vehicle in the area. This leaves the departing grav car unidentified; either the crew misread its colours, it was impersonating the POC, or the officers’ account is incomplete. These possibilities are unconfirmed
Ozy now holds potentially useful research data from Ujinka’s house, but its specific contents and significance remain undefined
The crew prioritised repairing Vlen’s comms while waiting for the meeting with Odoy
Pallod now officially identifies Darrian Jak as Vlen’s killer and confirms Jak is a short redhead. This is the POC’s claim, not yet independently verified by the crew
Pallod dismissed the grav car, Ujinka murder, and localised system failures as coincidences and ended the call quickly; the crew regard his response as suspicious
The last-dialled number recovered from Vlen’s comms belongs to Winter Shipping, providing a new lead to the logistics and loans company operating in both Credo City and Star Town
Winter Shipping publicly advertises no-questions-asked cargo purchases aimed at financially distressed ship crews
Research into Vlen’s impossible age produced no new information
The Alahir and its captain provide a new link to Pallod and to apparent offworlders operating in POC uniforms
The offworlders in POC uniforms could explain the grav car seen leaving Dancado despite the local officers’ denial that another POC unit was present; this is an inference, not confirmed
Imperial police may have displaced the local POC from the murder investigation, while the Zhodani-spy and state-security claims remain unverified rumours

End position

The crew are back at the Regina Down TAS Hostel on the day of their scheduled 10pm meeting with Detective Odoy at The Flotsam
Iaros Ujinka is confirmed dead. The surviving intruder is in POC custody after mentioning Ven Yasha during the crew’s brief questioning
Pallod Norrim claims that short, red-haired Darrian Jak murdered Vlen and treats the case as solved, but the crew do not trust his explanation
Ozy recovered Ujinka’s research data, although its contents remain unspecified, and extracted the last-dialled number from Vlen’s comms before the device became fully damaged
The last-dialled number belongs to Winter Shipping, a logistics and cargo-buying company operating in both Credo City and Star Town
Admiral Cassius learned of the Alahir, its captain’s meetings with Pallod, offworlders in POC uniforms, and rumours of an Imperial police takeover involving state security and a supposed Zhodani spy
Kostas remains injured at STR 3, DEX 9 and END 1

Priorities for next session

Investigate Winter Shipping, including its Credo City and Star Town operations and why Vlen called it
Meet Detective Odoy at The Flotsam at 10pm as arranged
Follow the Alahir, its captain’s relationship with Pallod, and the offworlders reportedly operating in POC uniforms
Test Pallod’s claim that Darrian Jak killed Vlen and clarify the state-security and Zhodani-spy rumours

session-2026-08-16.title: Session 2026-08-16
session-2026-08-16.content:
traveller sota session
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
Session date: 2026-08-16
Starting in-fiction date: 195-1105
Starting position
The crew are back at the Regina Down TAS Hostel on 195-1105, the day of their 10pm meeting with Detective Odoy at The Flotsam.

Iaros Ujinka is confirmed dead after the attack at Dancado. One attacker died; the survivor is in POC custody after mentioning Ven Yasha under questioning. The third man is still loose
A grav car apparently in POC colours left Dancado immediately after the attack; local officers deny any other POC unit was present
Pallod Norrim claims Darrian Jak, a short redhead, murdered Vlen Backett and treats the case as closed. The crew do not consider that proven and found his manner suspicious
Ozy holds research data recovered from Ujinka’s house (contents unspecified) and pulled the last-dialled number from Vlen’s comms before the device failed — it belongs to Winter Shipping
Admiral Cassius learned of the Alahir, its captain’s repeated meetings with Pallod, offworlders reportedly wearing POC uniforms, and rumours of an Imperial state-security takeover of the murder inquiry
Kostas Backett remains badly injured: STR 3, DEX 9, END 1
Ujinka’s request that the Event Horizon back Ujinka’s Research is still unanswered

Live notes

The crew split to work the Winter Shipping lead: Ozy to research the company and attempt a remote hack of its systems, while Kostas Backett goes to the premises in person to recon the building. Kostas is still badly injured (END 1)
Winter Shipping’s premises are two buildings, one either side of the fence between Credo City and Star Town. The crew are approaching from the Credo side
Kostas rolled well and located the offices. The Credo-side building is closed, with a notice directing callers to the Star Town offices, which are visible across the fence
A huge brute of a man entered the Credo-side building and emerged on the Star Town side — a crossing that is not supposed to be possible. This implies a connection or passage through the fence between the two buildings
Kostas and StClair scoped out the security system. It looks unsophisticated; the crew believe they could shut down the alarms if they decide to break in
Ozy successfully hacked Winter Shipping’s systems remotely, but found almost nothing of interest — suspiciously little. The crew suspect the real records sit on a separate, unconnected system
The Star Town side operates a launch that runs up to Regina Highport
Ozy found flight records showing that some of those launch runs take hours longer than the trip should
The crew decided against breaking in for now. Plan: cross into Star Town, walk into the Winter Shipping offices with a legitimate piece of business as cover, and see what they can learn face to face
Kostas Backett bought a dagger in Star Town for protection. Regina is Law Level 9, where all weapons are banned — carrying it is illegal anywhere on the moon. The crew judge Star Town lawless enough to carry it there, and Kostas intends to drop it before returning to Credo City
Inside, the Star Town Winter Shipping office is very fancy — far smarter than the surroundings suggest. Behind the desk is Marid, a very attractive receptionist
The legitimate business used as cover was the crew’s cargo from Yori: 3 tons of crystals and gems, bought for Cr54,000 and sold for Cr72,000 — a Cr18,000 profit. That is the Event Horizon’s entire 3-ton hold
The sale is to Winter Shipping itself. Olso, the crew’s Winter Shipping contact, will be picking the cargo up — giving the crew a legitimate reason to observe Winter Shipping personnel and their collection process
Admiral Cassius called Pallod Norrim to try to find out what happened to the surviving Dancado intruder taken into POC custody
Pallod Norrim is no longer taking the crew’s calls. Nothing was learned about the prisoner
The crew set off for the 10pm meeting with Detective Odoy at The Flotsam
Detective Odoy tells the crew he is investigating Ven Yasha, and that he believes Ven Yasha killed Vlen Backett — directly contradicting Pallod Norrim’s official line that Darrian Jak is the murderer. Odoy’s claim is unverified
Odoy’s theory is that Vlen was working as a courier for Ven Yasha. Unverified, but it would fit Vlen’s constant travel and improbable contacts
Further from Odoy (all his account, unverified):

No Zhodani spy was killed. The murder behind the rumour is Vlen, and he was not a spy — the spy story is a cover used to justify the Imperial police takeover of the inquiry
Imperial security have been everywhere on Regina
The Imperial force that arrived aboard the Alahir are after Ven Yasha
Odoy knows little about Iaros Ujinka or why she would be killed
The Dancado prisoner is no longer in POC custody — and the Imperial force also collected the other man from that attack
The red-haired man appears to be a fixer called Harlen, who is connected to Winter Shipping


Open question: Pallod Norrim named the short redhead as Darrian Jak and arrested him; Odoy names the red-haired man as Harlen. Whether Jak and Harlen are the same person, two different redheads, or an alias is not established

Decisions and discoveries

Winter Shipping occupies two buildings straddling the Credo City/Star Town fence, with an apparent internal passage between them — a man was seen entering one side and emerging on the other
The Credo-side office is closed and redirects callers to Star Town. Security on the premises is unsophisticated and the crew believe they could defeat the alarms
Winter Shipping’s networked systems hold almost nothing. The crew infer a second, unconnected system holding the real records — an inference, not confirmed
Winter Shipping runs a launch from the Star Town side to Regina Highport, and some of those runs take hours longer than the journey should. Unexplained
The crew sold their Yori cargo — 3 tons of crystals and gems — to Winter Shipping for Cr72,000 against a Cr54,000 outlay, using the sale as cover and a way to observe the company. Olso is the contact collecting it
Pallod Norrim has stopped taking the crew’s calls entirely. Nothing was learned about the Dancado prisoner through him
Detective Odoy gave a wholly different account of the case from Pallod’s. Everything below is Odoy’s claim and none of it is independently verified:

Ven Yasha, not Darrian Jak, killed Vlen Backett
Vlen was a courier for Ven Yasha
The Zhodani spy story is false. The murder it refers to is Vlen’s, and the spy framing exists to justify the Imperial police takeover of the inquiry
The Imperial force aboard the Alahir is hunting Ven Yasha, and Imperial security are all over Regina
Both Dancado attackers — the dead man and the prisoner — have been taken by that Imperial force. The prisoner is no longer in POC custody
The red-haired man is a fixer named Harlen, connected to Winter Shipping
Odoy has no explanation for Iaros Ujinka’s murder


Two independent sources now attach Ven Yasha to the case: the Dancado prisoner named him under questioning, and Odoy’s whole investigation is built on him
Unresolved identity: Pallod’s arrested suspect Darrian Jak and Odoy’s fixer Harlen are both short red-haired men tied to this murder. Whether they are the same man, an alias, or two people is not established
Harlen’s link to Winter Shipping ties the crew’s own recon to Odoy’s account: the same company took Vlen’s last call, employs a fixer matching the third man, and runs unexplained flights to the Highport
Odoy’s own agency, motives and reason for approaching the crew remain unrecorded

End position

The crew are at The Flotsam on the night of 195-1105, having just heard out Detective Odoy
The POC’s official case (Jak did it, case closed) and Odoy’s account (Yasha did it, the Imperials are hunting Yasha, the spy story is a cover) are in direct conflict. The crew have no way yet to test either
Pallod Norrim is unreachable; both Dancado attackers are beyond the crew’s reach in Imperial hands
Winter Shipping is now the strongest live lead: Vlen’s last call, Harlen’s employer, an internal fence crossing, a soft alarm system and unexplained Highport launches
The crew are up Cr18,000 on the Yori cargo, with the Event Horizon’s 3-ton hold empty pending collection by Olso
Kostas Backett remains injured at STR 3, DEX 9, END 1
Iaros Ujinka’s request that the Event Horizon back Ujinka’s Research is still unanswered

Priorities for next session

Break into Winter Shipping — the alarms look beatable; the targets are the second, unnetworked system, the passage between the two buildings, and anything on the Highport launch runs
Find out more about the Alahir — its captain, its crew, and the Imperial force Odoy says it carries
Try to meet Darrian Jak in prison — test Pallod’s case and settle whether Jak is Harlen

smashed-comms.title: Smashed Comms
smashed-comms.content:
traveller sota item clue
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
A smashed comms unit recovered from Vlen Backett’s room at the Regina Down TAS Hostel — the room the Three Men at Vlen’s Room walked into.
Whether it was smashed by hand or knocked out by The Device is unestablished. Either way, someone did not want its contents read.
Ozy made several repair attempts. Immediately before the unit became fully damaged and unusable, he recovered the last number called: it belongs to Winter Shipping, a logistics and cargo-buying company operating in Credo City and Star Town.
Notes

solomani-hypothesis.title: Solomani Hypothesis
solomani-hypothesis.content:
traveller sota clue
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
The theory that Humaniti originally evolved on the planet of Terra, home of the Solomani. According to it, The Ancients transplanted primitive humans to other worlds across the galaxy — most notably the homeworlds of the Vilani and the Zhodani.
Genetic evidence has largely confirmed it, though some scientists and religious groups advocate other origins for Humaniti, such as parallel evolution or divine intervention.
Why it’s in the file
Its confirmation is what gave rise to the Brotherhood of Humaniti — and the Brotherhood’s doctrine goes further, holding that the Ancients destroyed an ur-race of ‘true Humaniti’ when they split the species into tribes.
So the Ancients didn’t merely leave ruins in the Spinward Marches. They made the people currently arguing over those ruins.
Notes

spinward-marches.title: Spinward Marches
spinward-marches.content:
traveller sota location
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
Sector containing the Regina subsector, and within it Alell.
Ancients sites are especially common here — see The Ancients. The party are in the sector where the thing two people have been murdered over is buried.
Notes

startown.title: Startown
startown.content:
traveller sota location
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
The region around the old Regina starport, now the primary downport. A strip of bars, cheap hostelries, raucous entertainments and less savoury businesses — notoriously violent, corrupt and profitable.
Technically divided between the nearby cities of Credo and Atora; both blame the other for the state of it.
It is a thin strip between Credo and Atora. Winter Shipping operates here as well as in Credo City.
Regina Highport sits in geostationary orbit above Startown.
If The Flotsam is anywhere, this is the sort of district it would be in — unconfirmed.
Notes

the-ancients.title: The Ancients
the-ancients.content:
traveller sota species clue
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
Colloquial name for a species that lived 300,000 years ago. Comparatively little is known about them.
What they did

Believed responsible for transplanting Humaniti from its original homeworld of Terra (the Solomani Hypothesis) and scattering the species across hundreds of planets
Believed to have uplifted the Vargr from Terran canines
Exceedingly high technology — many artefacts are millennia beyond cutting-edge Imperial science. Estimates of high-end Ancients tech place them beyond TL25

Their sites
Several have been discovered across Charted Space, especially in the Spinward Marches — where the party currently are.

The technology at these sites varies considerably, suggesting different Ancients groups pursued radically different paths of development
Most sites show damage consistent with orbital bombardment or other violence
There are anomalies in other systems explicable only by weapons that destroyed entire planets
That, plus their sudden disappearance from known space, has produced the Ancients Extinction Theories
Ancients sites also show common use of Droyne as pets or servants

Why this matters here
Iaros Ujinka was tracing links between G-Band Transmissions and Ancients sites — see Ujinka’s Research. Vlen Backett was going to fund and crew the expedition. Both are now dead.
Threads worth holding together, none of them established:

Vlen was a man that Vargr crossed hundreds of parsecs to consult — and the Vargr are an Ancients-uplifted species
The Church of the Chosen Ones holds that Vargr are the rightful heirs of the Ancients
The Brotherhood of Humaniti holds that the Ancients broke humanity, and that institutions opposing its reunification must be destroyed
Vlen Backett’s True Age: at least 180 years old, physiologically 52, no anagathics. Nobody has explained that

Notes

the-device.title: The Device
the-device.content:
traveller sota clue
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
The third of the Three Men at Vlen’s Room — the red-haired one whose face was never caught — carried a device that appears to have caused electrical problems.
Recorded on the board with a question mark: the connection between the device and the interference is the party’s reading of the footage, not an established fact.
“What is this device that was used?” is one of the party’s active questions. It may also explain the Smashed Comms.
Possible second sighting
At Dancado, during the attack on Iaros Ujinka, the power was cut and a security drone taken out. Electrical systems failing at the exact moment of an attack — the same signature as the interference on the hostel footage.
If that’s the same device, the same crew is running both hits, and knocking out power and security is the opening move rather than a side effect.
Kostas Backett asked Pallod Norrim about the attackers’ apparent ability to disable systems in a localised area. Pallod dismissed it, the grav car and any connection between the murders as coincidence and nothing to worry about.
Notes

the-flotsam.title: The Flotsam
the-flotsam.content:
traveller sota location
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
A bar. Where Detective Odoy wants to meet the party at 10pm on 195-1105 — see Meeting at the Flotsam.
The crew intend to investigate Winter Shipping first, then attend the meeting as arranged.
Notes

three-men-at-vlen's-room.title: Three Men at Vlen's Room
three-men-at-vlen's-room.content:
traveller sota clue
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
Travellers’ Aid Society security camera footage from the Regina Down TAS Hostel — obtained and viewed by the party — shows three men going to Vlen Backett’s room.

Two are on camera. Heavy-set men, dark jackets. Neither identified.
The third’s face wasn’t seen, but he had red hair.
The third man was carrying a device — see The Device.

The two on the board are shown with question marks: the party has faces, not names.
Two identified at Dancado
At Dancado, two men came in through the front door and upstairs; one was killed and the other knocked unconscious and later taken into POC custody — clearly the same two men from the footage.
That confirms the two attacks are the work of the same crew. Before the authorities arrived, the surviving intruder mentioned Ven Yasha but gave little else.
The third man is still unaccounted for. A shooter stayed outside throughout and did not come in. Whether that’s the red-haired man with The Device is unestablished — but the attack opened the same way as the hostel job, with power and security knocked out first.
Pallod Norrim later said the POC had arrested Darrian Jak for Vlen’s murder and confirmed that Jak is short and red-haired. That matches the third man’s broad description, but it is not an independent identification.
Open questions

Who the two Dancado attackers were, and who sent them
Whether all three went into Vlen’s room, and how many came out
Whether the red-haired man deliberately kept off camera — see The Device
Whether the shooter who stayed outside at Dancado is the third man
Whether Darrian Jak is the red-haired third man or a convenient suspect

Notes

travellers'-aid-society.title: Travellers' Aid Society
travellers'-aid-society.content:
traveller sota faction
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
TAS. Vlen Backett was staying at their Regina Down TAS Hostel in Credo City when he was killed, and their security camera caught the Three Men at Vlen’s Room — so TAS holds the footage.
Expanded from “TAS” on the board; the board itself only ever writes the initials.
Notes

tusal.title: Tusal
tusal.content:
traveller sota item
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
An illegal narcotic, usually sold as tablets, though some prefer it in its less processed, undried form as a wad to be chewed. Derived from a seaweed.
Origin unknown, but believed to have been imported from the Vargr extents about a century ago. Now grown on various worlds along the Corridor sector.
Effects

A dose produces mild euphoria and intoxication
A very strong dose dulls pain receptors and causes unconsciousness
Users stay functional on a low dose, so many addicts chew six or seven tablets a day to hold a constant drugged haze

Who uses it
Especially associated with menial jobs and the unemployed — an otherwise dull life of drudgery made pleasant. Long-term addiction brings respiratory and digestive problems and a high incidence of stomach cancer.
Bearing on the murder
Vlen Backett had 200 ng/mL in his blood when he died — per the coroner, enough that he would barely have been able to stand, let alone fight back. That is squarely the “very strong dose” band: pain receptors dulled, heading for unconsciousness.
Two things that don’t fit a recreational user:

The drug’s user base is menial labourers and the unemployed holding a low functional dose. Vlen was neither, and his dose was nowhere near low.
A man that sedated doesn’t wander into a very strong dose by accident and then happen to be shot through the heart at close range with no defensive wounds.

It reads as a dose given to him to make the killing easy — inference, not established. See Vlen Backett’s Murder.
Darrian Jak sold a lot of Tusal in Credo City the night Vlen died — the party’s best lead on where this batch came from.
Loose thread
Tusal is believed to have come out of the Vargr extents. Vlen was a man that Vargr crossed hundreds of parsecs to consult. Probably nothing — the drug’s been in Imperial space a century and is grown locally — but it’s noted.
Notes

tyrus-cassius.title: Tyrus Cassius
tyrus-cassius.content:
traveller sota character
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
Admiral Tyrus Cassius — player character. Owns the Pinnace Implacable, carried by the Event Horizon.
Originally named Cmdr Valarian; renamed to Cassius. Anything recorded elsewhere under the old name refers to him.
Naval officer Kostas Backett served under. Led a mutiny that failed; Kostas backed it and was punished for it, Cassius apparently was not — he’s since retired as an Admiral. Kostas talked his way aboard the Event Horizon to find him and demand a job.
Aylin Boro, a retired admiral and one of Kostas’ contacts, hates him.
Appearance

Older man, greying dark hair, waxed moustache. Dark naval dress uniform — heavy gold braid at the cuffs, epaulettes, aiguillette, medal ribbons and orders at the breast — with a long greatcoat worn over the shoulders and his cap under one arm. Dressed for ceremony, not for work.
Notes

After the attack at Dancado, Cassius began tying up the unconscious intruder while the rest of the crew tried to restore the autodoc and retrieve Iaros Ujinka.
Cassius reported the Dancado attack to Chief Inspector Pallod Norrim.
He used his network to build influence on Regina beyond Pallod and learned about the Alahir, its captain’s repeated meetings with Pallod, and offworlders reportedly operating in POC uniforms.
His network also reported that an Imperial police force had taken over a murder inquiry as state security, with the dead man rumoured to have been a Zhodani spy. The claims remain unverified.

uakye.title: Uakye
uakye.content:
traveller sota location
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
Tidally locked, so all settlements sit in the habitable ‘twilight zone’.
Closely associated with Efate, but Countess Parasii strongly affirms her planet’s independence from “the technocracy one system over”.
Notes

ujinka's-research.title: Ujinka's Research
ujinka's-research.content:
traveller sota clue
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
Iaros Ujinka was investigating links between G-Band Transmissions and sites of Ancient technology. That’s what took her to Beck’s World, and it is what she and Vlen Backett were going to discuss.
Vlen’s involvement
Vlen was going to provide funding and a ship to support the research. That is the “topics of mutual interest” from his letter — and it means a drifter with no visible income was in a position to bankroll a university research programme and put a hull under it.
He was murdered before the meeting happened.
The proposal to the party
Before her death, Ujinka asked whether the party could use the Event Horizon to support the research instead. No final answer given yet.
The Event Horizon is a Lab Ship. She is, functionally, exactly the vessel this research needs — and Graxius StClair, who owns her, is Ujinka’s former student.
Worth knowing: Kaldi Research runs lab ships for hire throughout the Marches. Ujinka could have chartered a professional research vessel. She asked a dead man’s nephew’s crew instead.
Why this matters
Vlen agreed to fund and crew an expedition to Ancient sites, and was shot before he could. Ujinka was then shot dead in her own house, minutes after explaining the research to a second set of potential backers.
Two people, one project, both murdered inside four days. Someone is killing to stop this research — and they knew where and when to find her.
Who would care
Ancients sites cluster in the Spinward Marches, and their technology runs beyond TL25. A reliable method of finding those sites — which is what G-Band Transmissions would be — is worth killing for. Two movements on record already stake their theology on Ancients inheritance:

Church of the Chosen Ones — Vargr are the Ancients’ rightful heirs
Brotherhood of Humaniti — the Ancients broke humanity, and opposing institutions must be destroyed

Nobody has been placed at either murder.
What survives her

The party, who heard it from her directly
Data recovered by Ozy from her house at Dancado, concerning the Ancients research, Vlen and the g-band work. The GM has not yet specified its contents
Beck’s World, where the fieldwork was, and where Graxius StClair’s ex-wife still is
The University of Regina, her department
The Event Horizon, still the right ship for it, and the decision now nobody’s to accept

Notes

The crew have not yet decided whether to commit the Event Horizon to continuing the research.

university-of-regina.title: University of Regina
university-of-regina.content:
traveller sota faction
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
Commonly used to refer to any of several prestigious academic institutions on Regina. Collectively, the University of Regina is the largest and most successful higher-level education and research facility in the Spinward Marches.
Iaros Ujinka was a professor in its Department of History — until she was murdered. Her department, her colleagues and her papers are all still there, and are the obvious next place to look for whatever she knew about Ujinka’s Research.
Notes

vargr.title: Vargr
vargr.content:
traveller sota species
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
A species found outside the Imperium, in territory referred to as the Vargr extents. Tusal is believed to have been imported from there roughly a century ago.
Uplifted from Terran canines by The Ancients — which makes them one of the few living things with a direct claim on the Ancients’ legacy, and the Church of the Chosen Ones builds a whole theology on exactly that.
Vargr in the file so far

40th Squadron — organised Vargr power bloc in Gvurrdon, previously bankrolled by the Zhodani
Church of the Chosen Ones — fringe sect holding Vargr to be the Ancients’ rightful heirs
Menorb — agricultural world feeding the Vargr market, raided for it
Rynkatropa — a TL1 sophont species the Vargr enslaved
Tusal — the narcotic that killed Vlen Backett came out of the Vargr extents
Vargr once crossed hundreds of parsecs to consult Vlen himself

On at least one occasion, Vargr travelled hundreds of parsecs to consult Vlen Backett — the single strangest thing in his address book, and the clearest sign his interests reach well beyond Imperial space.
Notes

ven-yasha.title: Ven Yasha
ven-yasha.content:
traveller sota npc rival
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
Rival. A mysterious crime lord, wanted by numerous worlds around Regina. Location unknown.
No-one has ever seen them, so the wanted bulletins are extremely vague. Gender, species, whether “Ven Yasha” is even one person — all unknown.
Connection to Kostas
Kostas Backett has had plenty of issues throughout his career. Just the once, he put out feelers on who was behind one of them, and only one name came back.
Whispers from the shadows, a piece of paper found under a door, hushed exchanges with a contact — whatever went wrong and whenever he went looking for who was behind it, it was just a name and nothing more.
Connection to Vlen
His name kept cropping up in connection with Vlen Backett as well. Iaros Ujinka doesn’t know him personally, only by reputation — and says he is very unpleasant.
So the same name attaches to both Kostas’ career troubles and his murdered uncle’s affairs. That is either the single most important fact in the investigation or a coincidence of a very common bogeyman.
The surviving intruder from the attack at Dancado mentioned Ven Yasha during the crew’s brief questioning before the POC arrived. He gave little else, so the nature of the connection remains unknown.
Odoy’s account — 195-1105
Detective Odoy is investigating Ven Yasha, and told the crew that Yasha killed Vlen Backett and that Vlen was working as a courier for Yasha. He also says the Imperial force that arrived aboard the Alahir is on Regina hunting Yasha, with the Zhodani-spy story serving as cover for their takeover of the inquiry.
None of this is independently verified — it is Odoy’s word, and his own agency and motives are unknown. But it is now the second independent source naming Yasha: the surviving Dancado attacker did so too, before the Imperials removed him from POC custody.
If Odoy is right, the courier theory would explain Vlen’s constant travel and his improbable address book.
Open questions

Who is Ven Yasha?
If Vlen was his courier, what was Vlen carrying — and does it connect to Ujinka’s Research?
Why an Imperial force would cross to Regina to hunt him
How many of Kostas’ career problems are actually theirs? Only one was ever traced.
What the connection to Vlen actually is — creditor, rival, employer, killer?
Whether “he” is right: Ujinka uses it, but nobody has ever seen the man

Notes

vlen-backett's-murder.title: Vlen Backett's Murder
vlen-backett's-murder.content:
traveller sota clue
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
Vlen Backett was murdered in Credo City. From the coroner’s report:

Cause of death: low-velocity gunshot wound to the heart, delivered at close range
Defensive wounds: none
Blood test: 200 ng/mL of the narcotic Tusal — at that level he would barely have been able to stand, let alone fight back. That’s in the “very strong dose” band: pain receptors dulled, heading toward unconsciousness
Augmentations: none

Drugged first, then shot through the heart from close range, with no attempt to defend himself. That reads as an execution rather than a fight or a robbery gone wrong — inference, not stated in the report.
Low-velocity and close range also suggests a quiet weapon and someone who got near enough to use it — worth knowing whether Vlen let them get that close.
What the investigation has since established

Vlen arrived on Regina from Rhylanor three days before he died
He was staying at the Regina Down TAS Hostel, and their camera caught the Three Men at Vlen’s Room — two faces, and a third who kept off camera but had red hair
He was on Regina to meet Iaros Ujinka, a historian he already knew — a meeting arranged before he arrived, and one he never made
Iaros Ujinka has since been murdered too, at Dancado, minutes after explaining the same research to the party — and the party killed one of the two intruders and captured the other, both men from the hostel footage, tying the attacks to one crew
The meeting was to agree funding and a ship for Ujinka’s Research into Ancient technology sites. The first credible motive: he was about to put money and a hull behind an Ancients expedition
Ven Yasha’s name kept cropping up in connection with Vlen
The third carried The Device, which seems to have caused electrical interference
Darrian Jak, a local dealer, sold a lot of Tusal the night Vlen died. Pallod Norrim now claims the short, red-haired Jak killed Vlen, but the crew have not independently verified that conclusion
His Smashed Comms yielded one last number before becoming unusable: Winter Shipping
Admiral Cassius’s network reports that an Imperial police force has taken over a murder inquiry as a state-security matter, with the victim rumoured to be a Zhodani spy. Whether that inquiry and victim are Vlen’s is unconfirmed

Running state in Investigation Status.
Open questions

Who the three men are, and who sent them
Whether the Tusal was self-administered or given to him
Whether this is what the Regina Public Order Commission means by Irregularities in Vlen Backett’s Affairs, or something separate
What he was doing on Rhylanor, and whether he was followed from there
Whether Pallod’s case against Darrian Jak is genuine, mistaken or a cover story
Why Vlen’s last recovered call was to Winter Shipping

Notes

vlen-backett's-true-age.title: Vlen Backett's True Age
vlen-backett's-true-age.content:
traveller sota clue
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
The coroner’s report on Vlen Backett states:

Physiological age: 52
Historical records indicate true age at least 180
No sign of anagathics in his blood system
No augmentations

He was at least 180 years old, had the body of a 52-year-old, and there is no chemical explanation for it.
Every relative who knew him as “every child’s favourite uncle” knew a man who had been doing that for generations. Kostas Backett is 38.
Open questions

How
Whether he knew what he was
Whether it connects to his archaeology, his unnamed contacts among scientists and high nobility, or the Vargr who crossed hundreds of parsecs to consult him
Whether whoever killed him knew

Notes

Kostas researched Vlen’s age again before the meeting with Odoy but found nothing new.

vlen-backett.title: Vlen Backett
vlen-backett.content:
traveller sota npc ally
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
Ally. Murdered. “Uncle Vlen” — Kostas Backett’s extended family. Homeworld Alell.
Human. Physiologically 52 at death; historical records put his true age at at least 180, with no anagathics in his blood — see Vlen Backett’s True Age. Killed by a close-range gunshot to the heart while drugged senseless — see Vlen Backett’s Murder.
Took Kostas under his wing plenty of times throughout his troubled career — without Vlen’s “loans” he may never have made it. The scare quotes are the character sheet’s own; on what terms is unstated.
Character
Only at home when travelling. He’d visit Alell for a few weeks or a month or two, delighting friends and family with tales of distant planets and exotic cultures, then the wanderlust would take him off again. A charming old rogue — the more staid relatives disapproved of his questionable, unreliable ways, but he was every child’s favourite uncle.
What he actually does
No-one was ever sure, or whether he was just a drifter amid the stars.

Worked tramp traders, signed on as a deckhand on freighters
Dabbled in archaeology and journalism
Never liked to talk about it, but had quite a collection of firearms and could handle himself in a fight

His strange friends
Mostly other space voyagers — but he received irregular communications from scientists, naval officers, corporate oligarchs, even high nobility. On at least one occasion, Vargr from outside the Imperium travelled hundreds of parsecs to consult with him.
That detail reads differently now: the Vargr were uplifted by The Ancients, Vlen was funding a hunt for Ancients sites, and he was killed with a narcotic that came out of the Vargr extents.
None of these contacts are named. The archaeology plus the reach of that address book is a lot of smoke for a man with no visible job — worth pulling on.
What he was doing on Regina
He came to meet Iaros Ujinka and agree terms on Ujinka’s Research — he was going to provide the funding and a ship for an expedition to sites of Ancient technology. He was killed three days after arriving, before the meeting happened.
Ven Yasha’s name kept cropping up in connection with him.
The last recoverable call from his smashed comms was to Winter Shipping, a logistics and cargo-buying company operating in Credo City and Star Town.
Death
Murdered in Credo City on Regina, late of Regina/Alell. The coroner’s report gives the details (Vlen Backett’s Murder, Vlen Backett’s True Age); the Commission’s letter, below, never mentions that he was killed at all. Notified to Kostas Backett by Pallod Norrim of the Regina Public Order Commission — Handout 2, “Message from Regina”, sealed 190 Standard, 1105 Third Imperium.

Before his death, Vlen left instructions on file with the Public Order Commission naming Kostas as next of kin — to resolve his outstanding affairs on Regina, take possession of his belongings, and transport his remains back to Alell.
A sum of money is deposited with the First Ducal Bank to cover expenses.
His body is in a cryogenic facility in Credo City, to be transferred to Kostas as soon as possible. A TL14+ autodoc can reanimate a corpse kept in a low berth or cryoberth for up to 1D days after death — Vlen died on or before 190-1105 and it is now 193. Probably outside the window, and no one has raised it, but the body is in cryo and Kostas is the legal next of kin who takes possession of it.
Kostas is required, in the name of the Duke and under the Public Order Act of 527 (Amended), to travel to Regina with all due haste — or reply so alternate arrangements can be made.
“Given certain irregularities with Vlen Backett’s affairs, it is vitally important that you contact the Public Order Commission upon arrival.” See Irregularities in Vlen Backett’s Affairs.

Two oddities in the letter itself: it’s addressed to the “chattels and corpus of Vlen Backett (deceased)” rather than to Kostas by name, and the Chief Inspector signs off as Pallod Norum having opened as Pallod Norrim.
Pallod now claims that short, red-haired Darrian Jak murdered Vlen and considers the case closed. The crew have not independently verified that conclusion and distrust Pallod’s dismissal of the connected events at Dancado.
The courier theory
On 195-1105 Detective Odoy told the crew that Vlen was a courier for Ven Yasha, and that Yasha killed him — not Jak. Odoy also says the rumour of a murdered Zhodani spy refers to Vlen, that Vlen was not a spy, and that the story is a cover for the Imperial takeover of the inquiry.
All unverified. It would, though, account for a man with no visible job, constant travel, and an address book running from scientists to high nobility — and it sits alongside his last recovered call going to Winter Shipping, where Odoy places the fixer Harlen.
Unresolved: whether courier work and the funding of Ujinka’s Research are the same thread or two separate lives.
Notes

whisperhawk.title: Whisperhawk
whisperhawk.content:
traveller sota species
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
An animal. One of the most common sights in the Alell jungle — beautiful avians with prodigious wingspans.
Their wings are both locomotion and feeding organs: whisperhawks feed by digesting the insects caught on the sticky undersides. A flock gliding across the canopy at twilight catches hundreds of thousands of insects; the buzzing of the trapped insects and the susurrus of the wind gives the whisperhawk its name.
They are notoriously stupid and have been known to attack humans and vehicles, as well as flagposts, fences, houses and small trees. If threatened, a whisperhawk attacks by wrapping its wings around a larger foe and trying to smother it.
Notes

winter-shipping.title: Winter Shipping
winter-shipping.content:
traveller sota faction
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
A logistics and cargo-buying company operating in both Credo City and Star Town, the thin strip between Credo and Atora.
The last number called from Vlen Backett’s smashed comms belongs to Winter Shipping. Ozy recovered the number immediately before the damaged device became unusable.
Its advertising targets ship crews struggling with mortgage payments, salaries or repair bills. It offers to buy their cargo with the promise: “Prompt service. No questions asked.”

The premises — reconnoitred 195-1105
Two buildings, one either side of the fence between Credo City and Star Town. The crew approached from the Credo side.

The Credo-side building is closed, with a notice directing callers to the Star Town offices
A huge brute of a man was seen entering the Credo side and emerging on the Star Town side — a crossing that is not supposed to be possible. The crew infer an internal passage through the fence; unconfirmed
The Star Town office interior is very fancy, far smarter than its surroundings. Marid works reception
StClair and Kostas Backett judged the security system unsophisticated — the crew believe they could shut down the alarms

Systems and the launch

Ozy hacked the company’s systems remotely and found almost nothing of interest — suspiciously little. The crew infer a second, unconnected system holding the real records; unconfirmed
The Star Town side operates a launch running up to Regina Highport
Flight records show some of those runs take hours longer than the trip should. Unexplained

Dealings with the crew
On 195-1105 the crew sold their Yori cargo — 3 tons of crystals and gems, bought for Cr54,000 — to Winter Shipping for Cr72,000, using the sale as cover and as a reason to watch the company work. Olso is the contact collecting it.
Connection to Harlen
Detective Odoy says the red-haired man in the case is a fixer called Harlen, connected to Winter Shipping. Odoy’s account is unverified, but it puts the company at the centre of the murder as well as at the end of Vlen’s last call.
Open questions

Why Vlen called the company
Whether the call concerned cargo, money, transport or something else
Who at Winter Shipping spoke to him
What the second system holds, and what the overlong launch runs are doing
What Harlen does here, and whether the company is Ven Yasha’s

Notes

The crew intend to investigate Winter Shipping before meeting Detective Odoy at The Flotsam.
After the Odoy meeting, the crew decided to break in — targets being the unnetworked system, the passage between the buildings, and the launch records.

wochiers.title: Wochiers
wochiers.content:
traveller sota location
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
Atmospheric pressure at sea level is more than four bars, so the population lives in the mountains or in underground complexes.
That high pressure makes Wochiers ideal for certain engineering projects, especially crystal growing.
By tradition, all visitors must bring an offering of a living plant to the hydroponics caves. Suitable plants are available in the starport gift shop.
Notes

yori.title: Yori
yori.content:
traveller sota location
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
Where the party were before this. They left on 185-1105 and arrived at Regina on 193-1105.
They left because of the Regina Public Order Commission’s notice of Vlen Backett’s death — though the GM’s timeline dates that notice five days after the departure. Assumed to be a date slip rather than a mystery.
Notes

yres.title: Yres
yres.content:
traveller sota location
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
The only surface structure is the entrance to the starport — an extremely impressive system of airlocks and tubes reaching from the surface to the seabed. The cities of this balkanised world are all underground and underwater.

Visitors face an additional docking fee of Cr250, an obligatory donation to the Yres Reconstruction and War Widows Fund
The atmosphere is highly radioactive; iodine tablets are available from public dispensers throughout the cities

A reconstruction fund and a war widows fund implies a war worth reconstructing from.
Notes

zena-antonia.title: Zena Antonia
zena-antonia.content:
traveller sota npc
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
Receptionist at the Regina Down TAS Hostel — where Vlen Backett was staying when he was killed, and where the party are now staying themselves.
She and Kostas Backett have been lightly flirting.
After Kostas was shot at Dancado, he tried to use the injury to win her sympathy. It did not work.
She was not on duty the night Vlen died — that was a different receptionist, since traced and interviewed, who had nothing useful to offer.
The desk sees everyone who comes and goes. She is the closest thing the party have to a source inside the building the murder happened in, and Kostas is the one talking to her.
Notes

zhodani.title: Zhodani
zhodani.content:
traveller sota species
Traveller Secrets of the Ancients
A power hostile to, or at least rivalrous with, the Imperium. They have previously propped up the 40th Squadron to threaten the Imperium’s flank.
Nothing else established in play yet.
Notes
